result.title: Demystifying On-Policy Distillation: Where Does the Teacher's Advantage Live?
result.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) is increasingly studied as a cheaper alternative to reinforcement learning, yet it remains a form of knowledge distillation (KD) that relies on teacher supervision. We revisit OPD from the KD perspective by asking where the teacher's advantage lies along student-generated trajectories. Controlled token flips at teacher-student disagreements directly measure the accuracy gained from teacher corrections. Single-token flips yield a modest average gain on selected failed trajectories, whereas repeated flips raise accuracy from 28.4% to 74.5%, close to the teacher's 76.9%. Gains continue to accumulate with more flips, but mass- and KL-based selection outperform random flips by 15-18 percentage points at counts of similar magnitude. Selective intervention remains useful after OPD, but greater argmax agreement does not consistently improve accuracy across model pairs. We advocate training schedules that learn more valuable teacher corrections while maintaining distributional stability. Controlled flips and fork-resolution analysis evaluate OPD beyond accuracy by measuring which teacher preferences the student acquires and what further correction can recover.

AI.brief_summary: 论文从知识蒸馏视角重新审视 on-policy distillation，在师生分歧的位置做受控 token 翻转，量化教师纠正带来的准确率增益，并比较按 mass、KL 与随机方式选择纠正点的效果，还分析了 OPD 之后干预是否仍有价值及其与 argmax 一致性的关系。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「翻转—增益」的因果式贡献测量与选择性监督设计，可能可供核查 LVR 训练中轨迹监督的价值分配、教师信号筛选与何时停止纠正，但属纯文本蒸馏场景，需确认能否迁移到 latent 状态监督。
